writing.sample_en:
【参考范文 · 179 词】写作无唯一标准答案，以下为达标示范
Nowadays more and more people choose to live an environmentally friendly lifestyle. This shift is no longer a slogan but a set of daily habits that reshape how we eat, travel and consume.
Several concrete practices explain this trend. To begin with, many commuters now favour buses, subways or shared bikes over private cars, which cuts carbon emission and eases traffic. What is more, sorting rubbish into recyclable and kitchen waste has become routine in my own neighbourhood, so that plastic and paper can be recycled rather than buried. Take myself as an example: since I started carrying a cloth bag and a reusable bottle, I have thrown away far less single-use plastic every week. Small as these acts seem, they add up to a sustainable way of living.
As a result, an environmentally friendly lifestyle benefits both individuals and the planet. It saves resources, keeps the air cleaner and reminds us that a green future depends on the choices we make today. I firmly believe that when everyone takes one small step, the earth will thank us tomorrow.

lines.en: W: Mr. David Jackson, a staff writer at the New Yorker, is known for his non-fiction books of adventure. Today, we go on a different kind of adventure: Jackson's life of parenting his offspring. David, as a parent of an 11- and a 14-year-old, what is the most interesting issue you are dealing with right now?
lines.zh: W: 大卫·杰克逊先生是《纽约客》的一名专职撰稿人，以创作冒险类非虚构作品而闻名。今天，我们要进行一次不同类型的冒险：杰克逊养育子女的生活。大卫，作为一个有一名11岁和一名14岁孩子的家长，你目前正在面对的最有趣的问题是什么？

lines.en: M: It's easy to focus on the challenges, but so far, I find these ages to be kind of wonderful. They are independent, and they have their own curiosities and obsessions. You can talk to them about fairly sophisticated subject matter such as politics.
lines.zh: M: 人们很容易把注意力集中在挑战上，但到目前为止，我觉得这个年龄段还是相当美好的。他们很独立，也有自己的好奇心和痴迷点。你可以和他们谈论政治之类相当复杂的话题。

lines.en: W: Yes, that does sound refreshing compared with talking to younger children. Do they ask you to proofread their essays?
lines.zh: W: 是的，和年幼的孩子交谈相比，这听起来确实令人耳目一新。他们会让你帮忙校对作文吗？

lines.en: M: Certainly, with writing they do. I really just try to be encouraging. I think at this age, editorial guidance is less important than encouragement.
lines.zh: M: 会的，写作方面他们确实会。我真的只是尽量给予鼓励。我认为，在这个年龄段，编辑方面的指导不如鼓励重要。

lines.en: W: Are there books that you think are important that your children read, and that all children read?
lines.zh: W: 有没有一些你认为很重要、应该让你的孩子读，也应该让所有孩子读的书？

lines.en: M: My general thought is to read widely and to incorporate a love for reading. Learning to love to read, I think, is the optimal thing, because it gives you a skill you can take anywhere.
lines.zh: M: 我的总体想法是广泛阅读，并培养对阅读的热爱。我认为，学会热爱阅读是最理想的事情，因为这会赋予你一种可以带到任何地方的技能。

lines.en: W: So you're not too concerned like some parents with the content they're reading? I know I have some worries about that.
lines.zh: W: 所以，你不像一些家长那样太在意他们阅读的内容？我知道自己对此有些担忧。

lines.en: M: Yeah, read what you like. If a child loves graphic novels or comic books, whatever it is, that is turning them on to read and turning on their imagination.
lines.zh: M: 是的，喜欢读什么就读什么。如果孩子喜欢图像小说或漫画书，不管是什么，只要能让他们喜欢上阅读，激发他们的想象力就好。

lines.en: W: I feel that children's tastes in books change as they reach adolescence. I know that mine certainly did when I was a teenager. What do you think?
lines.zh: W: 我觉得，随着孩子步入青春期，他们对书籍的品味会发生变化。我知道自己十几岁时确实发生过这种变化。你怎么看？

lines.en: M: I think it's especially important as they get older to read subject matter that'll open their eyes to the world and people. So I think both fiction and non-fiction are really important because they give you the power to begin to perceive the world through the lives of others.
lines.zh: M: 我认为，随着他们年龄增长，阅读一些能让他们开阔眼界、了解世界和他人的内容尤其重要。所以我觉得，小说和非虚构作品都非常重要，因为它们赋予你一种力量，让你开始通过他人的人生来感知这个世界。

transcripts.head: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

lines.en: M: In this episode of Money Talks, our guest is Molly Sanders, a university student and a successful young entrepreneur. Molly, tell us about your business.
lines.zh: M：在本期《金钱访谈》中，我们的嘉宾是莫莉·桑德斯，一名大学生，也是一位成功的年轻企业家。莫莉，给我们介绍一下你的生意吧。

lines.en: W: Well, I sell specialty clothes through a website, mainly for women who have trouble finding suitable clothes in main street shops because of their height or weight. But I do some men's clothes too.
lines.zh: W：嗯，我通过一个网站销售特色服装，主要面向那些因为身高或体重而难以在商业街服装店找到合适衣服的女性。不过，我也做一些男装。

lines.en: M: How did you get started in this business at such a young age? Are you studying fashion design?
lines.zh: M：你这么年轻，是怎么开始做这门生意的？你在学习服装设计吗？

lines.en: W: Actually, I'm majoring in finance, but I've always loved clothes. And I started making my own at 14.
lines.zh: W：其实，我的专业是金融，但我一直很喜欢服装。而且我从14岁起就开始自己做衣服了。

lines.en: M: Did you have any sort of training in design or sewing? Or was it a natural ability?
lines.zh: M：你接受过设计或缝纫方面的培训吗？还是说这是你的天赋？

lines.en: W: I'd have to say no to both. No one taught me to make clothes and most of the things I made at first were disasters.
lines.zh: W：这两方面都不是。没人教过我做衣服，而且我刚开始做的大多数衣服都糟糕透了。

lines.en: M: Why did you persevere? I think most people would give up if they kept failing, especially at that age.
lines.zh: M：你为什么坚持下来了？我想大多数人如果一直失败，都会放弃，尤其是在那个年纪。

lines.en: W: I kept on out of necessity. As you can see, I'm very tall and I couldn't find clothes that fit me in ordinary shops. So I kept trying and developed my skills over time.
lines.zh: W：我是出于需要才坚持下来的。你也看得出来，我个子很高，在普通商店里找不到合身的衣服。所以我不断尝试，随着时间的推移逐渐提高了自己的技能。

lines.en: M: Well, my notes say you earned $50,000 in profits last year, an extraordinary amount for a 20-year-old student. How did that happen? Did you see a gap in the market and decide to fill it?
lines.zh: M：嗯，我的资料上说，你去年赚了5万美元的利润。对于一名20岁的学生来说，这是一笔惊人的数目。这是怎么做到的？你发现了市场空缺，然后决定填补它吗？

lines.en: W: No. When I started university, some classmates complimented my clothes. And when I said I made them myself, other tall women started asking if I would make theirs. And I did. And before I knew it, I was an entrepreneur.
lines.zh: W：不是。我上大学时，一些同学夸我的衣服好看。当我说衣服是我自己做的之后，其他高个子女性开始问我能不能帮她们做衣服。我答应了。没过多久，我就成了一名企业家。

lines.en: M: So what are your plans for the future? Do you intend to open a physical store?
lines.zh: M：那么，你对未来有什么计划？你打算开一家实体店吗？

lines.en: W: No. I'll keep things online to keep costs down. But I will add more clothes for children, both girls and boys, and possibly even for infants. And I hope to add to my range of designs for men.
lines.zh: W：不打算。我会继续在线经营，以降低成本。不过，我会增加更多儿童服装，包括女孩和男孩的服装，甚至可能还会做婴儿服装。我也希望增加男装的设计种类。

lines.en: Researchers have identified a potent new antibiotic compound using artificial intelligence. The antibiotic can kill very dangerous bacteria. According to a study published in the journal Cell, the compound successfully removed deadly strains of bacteria in mice which are resistant to all known antibiotics.
lines.zh: 研究人员利用人工智能发现了一种强效的新型抗生素化合物。这种抗生素能够杀死极其危险的细菌。根据发表在《细胞》杂志上的一项研究，该化合物成功清除了小鼠体内对所有已知抗生素都具有耐药性的致命细菌菌株。

lines.en: The researchers say this is the first time that artificial intelligence has been used to find a powerful new antibiotic molecule. Why does this matter? The answer is antibiotic resistance. This happens when bacteria develop the ability to survive the medications designed to kill them. Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat to health and the problem is growing. This makes finding new antibiotics very important. However, in recent decades, very few have been developed, and those that have tend to be very similar to drugs already available. The searches also tend to only focus on a narrow spectrum of chemical compounds, but this is where artificial intelligence comes in. Why? To find new drugs, scientists screen molecules to predict how effective they might be. Typically, such screening is done by humans in the lab, which is both costly and slow. Artificial intelligence is different. It's fast, and it can process a high volume. It can screen hundreds of millions of compounds to identify a few interesting candidates that require experimental testing. Artificial intelligence is also able to predict if compounds are likely to be toxic. Some experts assert that this work signifies a paradigm shift in antibiotic discovery. It could change drug discovery more generally.
lines.zh: 研究人员表示，这是人工智能首次被用于寻找一种强效的新型抗生素分子。这为什么很重要？答案是抗生素耐药性。当细菌产生在为杀死它们而设计的药物作用下存活的能力时，就会出现这种情况。抗生素耐药性对健康构成严重威胁，而且这一问题正在加剧。因此，寻找新的抗生素至关重要。然而，近几十年来，开发出的新抗生素寥寥无几，而且那些已经开发出的通常与现有药物非常相似。这些搜索也往往只关注范围狭窄的化合物，但这正是人工智能发挥作用的地方。为什么？为了寻找新药，科学家会筛选分子，预测它们可能具有多大疗效。通常，这种筛选由实验室中的人类完成，既成本高昂又耗时缓慢。人工智能则不同。它速度快，而且能够处理海量数据。它可以筛选数亿种化合物，找出少数值得关注、需要进行实验测试的候选物。人工智能还能够预测化合物是否可能具有毒性。一些专家认为，这项工作标志着抗生素发现领域的范式转变。它也可能从总体上改变药物研发。

lines.en: A recent study overturned what we think we know about lying. Most of us have a theory about how to tell if someone is telling a lie. We may develop that theory from observations of those people we know well and see regularly, but we tend to generalize what we gather from that unscientific daily research and make it a universal theory.
lines.zh: 一项最新研究推翻了我们对说谎的固有认识。我们大多数人都有一套判断某人是否在说谎的理论。这套理论可能源于我们对熟悉且经常见面的人的观察，但我们往往会把从这种不科学的日常观察中得出的结论加以概括，并将其视为普遍适用的理论。

lines.en: So we might imagine that liars have evasive eyes, or the opposite—they simply stare at you. Or perhaps it is more generally nervous behavior we associate with lies. Whatever the particular theory, it's usually based on close observation of people we know. And we get lots of practice. On average, we're lied to some 200 times per day. These are mostly harmless lies, but lies nonetheless.
lines.zh: 因此，我们可能会认为说谎者目光闪躲，或者恰恰相反，他们只是盯着你看。又或者，我们通常会把某种更普遍的紧张行为与谎言联系起来。无论具体是哪一种理论，它通常都建立在对我们熟悉的人的细致观察之上。而且，我们有大量的实践机会。平均而言，我们每天大约会被欺骗200次。这些大多是无害的谎言，但归根结底仍然是谎言。

lines.en: But there's a problem with our theories, even though they're based on all these observations. The average person—you and me—tested rigorously on how well we detect lies fails to do better than chance. That's well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies. It's even relatively easy to fool lie detectors, the gold standard of lie detection, by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
lines.zh: 然而，尽管我们的理论建立在所有这些观察之上，它们仍然存在一个问题。普通人，也就是你我，在接受严格测试以评估识别谎言的能力时，表现并不比凭猜测好。这一点已经被众多研究以及研究人员为找出可靠的测谎方法所进行的大量尝试充分证实。即使是测谎的金标准测谎仪，也相对容易被欺骗，只要通过训练掌握呼吸技巧并抑制相关生理反应即可。

lines.en: Is there any way to get better at detecting lies? The new research offers some surprising advice. Stop looking and listen instead. It turns out that if we're unable to see the face, but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.
lines.zh: 有没有办法提高识别谎言的能力？这项新研究给出了令人意外的建议：不要再看，而是改为倾听。事实证明，如果我们看不到对方的脸，而是专注于相关人士的声音，我们的准确率会显著提高。

lines.en: Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful and undemanding; show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless. Don't challenge anyone with authority unless you are famous or very rich.
lines.zh: 表现得顺从、谦卑、感恩而且毫无要求；即使医生来你的病房只是短暂逗留且毫无用处，也要表现出极大的喜悦。除非你名声显赫或非常富有，否则不要挑战任何有权威的人。

lines.en: Those are a few strategies for dealing with today's American medical establishment. What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that. In his book, A Whole New Life, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord. It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
lines.zh: 这些是应对当今美国医疗机构的几种策略。患者想要的是受到尊重和体贴的对待。但依我的经验，愿意这样做的医院和医生太少了。小说家雷诺兹·普莱斯在其著作《全新的生活》中回忆说，他的医生选择了一条拥挤的走廊作为告诉他脊髓上可能长有肿瘤的地点。两位医生都没有想到，走廊并不是传达这一特殊消息最恰当的地方。

lines.en: My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired. He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice. He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
lines.zh: 我的外科医生三十多岁，看起来很疲惫。他一直被那些在冬季结冰路面上摔倒的患者弄得应接不暇。他是个风趣的人，但有时他的幽默并不受欢迎。

lines.en: "The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon," he tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week. I'm terrified because I have no idea where to go. I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches. The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot. But my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon. "I have to work with these people," he tells my friend, Dr. Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
lines.zh: “医疗保险公司蓝十字希望我明天下午把你赶到雪地里去，”我住院一个多星期后，他对我说。我吓坏了，因为我完全不知道该去哪里。我无法行走，甚至连腿抬高几英寸都做不到。医院的社会工作者让我觉得她是个笨蛋。但我对她的抱怨只让我的外科医生感到恼火。“我还得和这些人共事，”当我的朋友凯伦·布鲁德尼医生出面替我求情，并安排把我转到另一家医院时，他对她说道。

lines.en: "If you say one negative thing, they get defensive," she tells me later. "They have this kind of institutional loyalty. Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better. And," Brudney adds, "if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult. They want you to be totally passive. The entire health care system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients. Patients are incidental."
lines.zh: “只要你说一句负面的话，他们就会采取防御姿态，”她后来对我说。“他们有一种机构忠诚感。一定要带一位代言人，也就是说，带另一个人和你一起去医院，并把每一个问题及其答案、每一位医生和护士的姓名全都记下来。当人们知道你记住了他们的名字时，他们的表现会好一些。而且，”布鲁德尼补充道，“如果作为患者，你表示希望对哪怕一部分情况进行掌控，或者希望被征求意见、被告知情况，那么你就会被视为难相处的人。他们希望你完全被动。整个医疗保健体系，尤其是医院和养老院的存在，都是出于与照料患者毫无关系的原因。患者只是附带的存在。”

lines.en: There are probably teams you've worked with but you never want to work with again. But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally. In other words, your team had vitality. Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
lines.zh: 你可能曾与一些团队共事过，但再也不想与他们合作。然而，肯定也有一些其他团队，是你非常珍视能在职业上与之重聚的。换句话说，你的团队具有活力。当人们与团队同事建立的联系使他们即使在团队解散后仍保持联系时，团队就会产生这种活力。

lines.en: What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together? This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.
lines.zh: 团队具有什么样的特征，才能使其成员即使不再一起工作，也更有可能保持联系？最近，一项发表于商业期刊的研究回答了这个问题。

lines.en: One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness. Specifically, sharing the same gender or ethnic origin. The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they will be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose. After ties are established, similarity strengthens them. As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration. In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others. Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful. Yet, we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different. If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you'll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
lines.zh: 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是相似性，具体来说，就是拥有相同的性别或族裔背景。一个团队成员的人口统计特征越相似，他们就越倾向于在团队完成使命很久之后仍保持同事关系。联系建立之后，相似性会进一步巩固这种联系。因此，他们会更加信任并相互理解这些人，这促使他们寻求进一步合作的机会。实际上，人们往往会与相似的人建立更牢固、更持久的联系。与我们外貌和声音不同的人，或许拥有帮助我们取得更大成功所需的资源。然而，仅仅因为他们与众不同，我们就会发现自己明显不那么信任他们。如果你是职场多元化的坚定倡导者，毫无疑问会对这样的发现感到震惊。

lines.en: The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members. The more they trust one another, share the same goals and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections, despite no longer working as one team. Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it's safe to take risks with each other, and their members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
lines.zh: 研究人员确定的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。他们彼此越信任，目标越一致，并且越依赖彼此来实现这些目标，即使不再作为一个团队工作，他们维持彼此联系的可能性就越大。关系良好的团队拥有一种共同信念，即彼此合作承担风险是安全的；其成员也有义务分担工作量并互相提供帮助。

lines.en: From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies. The truth is some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again. The inconsistency, though, is that I've never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I am a member right now. And yet, the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically. So I am unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.
lines.zh: 根据个人经历，我既能看出这类研究的真实性，也能看出其中的不一致之处。真实之处在于，我最亲密的一些友谊源于我们曾一起在团队中工作，而我也会主动寻找再次与他们合作的机会。然而，不一致之处在于，我从未在一个比我目前所在团队更加成功、更加团结的团队中工作过。可是，我们四个人几乎没有共同之处，在人口统计特征上也完全不同。因此，我不太可能质疑多元化劳动力的价值。

transcripts.head: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

lines.en: An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors. She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income. These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus and social indifference.
lines.zh: 一位研究了6亿名百万富翁的美国研究人员发现，一个人能够变得多么富有，归根结底取决于六个财富因素。她发现，无论年龄或收入如何，六种行为都与净资产潜力有关。这些行为分别是节俭、自信、责任感、规划、专注以及不在意社会评价。

lines.en: Being thrifty comes as no great surprise. Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck. "Even with an astronomical level of income," she wrote, "to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%."
lines.zh: 节俭并不令人感到意外。入不敷出地消费、不为退休储蓄而消费、预想着自己会变得富有而消费，都会使你沦为薪水的奴隶。她写道：“即使收入达到天文数字，要想合理地积累财富，专家也建议将收入的20%存起来，靠剩下的80%生活。”

lines.en: Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty. It takes confidence to live within your means. It also takes confidence to invest properly. Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan. But people can't invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes. Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn't acquire their wealth through luck. Millionaires don't count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don't blame anyone else if they fall short. They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves. They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through. 92% of the millionaires surveyed developed a long term plan for their money and 97% almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
lines.zh: 拥有自信是另一个关键特征，因为这能帮助人们保持节俭。量入为出需要自信。正确地进行投资同样需要自信。财务规划师建议，不要凭情绪做出投资决定，而应放任投资自行运作，并专注于长期投资计划。但如果不对结果承担责任，人们就无法投资或管理自己的资金。许多百万富翁都承担个人责任，而且大多数人还碰巧是白手起家，这意味着他们并非靠运气获得财富。百万富翁不会指望别人让自己变得富有，如果没有达到目标，他们也不会责怪别人。他们专注于自己能够控制的事情，并使日常习惯与自己设定的目标保持一致。他们往往以目标为导向且勤奋努力，这使他们能够进行财务规划，并专注于贯彻落实这些计划。接受调查的百万富翁中，有92%为自己的资金制定了长期计划，97%几乎总能实现自己设定的目标。

lines.en: And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent. They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more. Essentially, they don't yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired. Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they're focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.
lines.zh: 正是这些行为，使他们很容易做到不在意社会评价。他们抵制生活方式膨胀，也就是一个人收入增加后便倾向于增加消费。他们基本不会屈服于购买最新产品的压力，也不会为了与他人保持一致或追赶他人已经拥有的东西而消费。他们关注的不是今天可能让自己感到快乐的事物，而是长期积累财富的计划。

analysis.定位: P2 What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration. But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that. 病人想要的是被尊重、被体谅地对待。但据我的经验，愿意这样做的医院和医生太少了。
analysis.信号: 转折 But + 程度词 too few。答案落在转折词后：But in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that。前半句说『病人想被尊重』是铺垫，But 之后才是主讲人的真实判断——能做到的医院太少，这正是定性句。

questions.stem: 【题目】 What does Karen Brudney suggest patients do?
questions.stem_zh: Karen Brudney建议病人做什么?

analysis.定位: P5 Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse. When people know you have their names, they behave better. 一定要带一个能为你说话的人，也就是任何别的人，陪你去医院，并且把每一个问题和答案、每一位医生和护士的名字都写下来。当别人知道你掌握着他们的名字时，他们就会表现得更好。
analysis.信号: 建议句信号 Always / write down。建议落在祈使句信号词上：Always bring an advocate 和 write down ... the name of every doctor and nurse。Always 开头的祈使句、write down 都是典型的建议语气，是答案句的标志。
analysis.替换: write down ... the name of every doctor and nurse↔Note down the names of all the doctors and nurses.同义词替换 write down=Note down

passages.en: The city of Bath was founded by the Romans almost two thousand years ago. It has been famous for its __(26)__ pleasing architecture and healing thermal springs ever since.
passages.zh: 巴斯城由罗马人于近两千年前建立。此后，它一直以美观宜人的建筑和具有疗愈功效的温泉而闻名。

passages.en: There are three hot springs in Bath; one is the King's Spring, upon which the Roman Baths and a temple were __(27)__ . The other two are the Cross Spring and the Hetling Spring, close to each other in Hot Bath Street. Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries to make use of the __(29)__ waters.
passages.zh: 巴斯有三处温泉，其中一处是国王泉，罗马浴场和一座神庙就建在这处泉水之上。另外两处是克罗斯泉和赫特林泉，二者彼此相距很近，位于温泉街。尽管巴斯主要以罗马风格和乔治亚风格的城市著称，但在此期间的几个世纪里，仍有许多人前来利用这里的天然泉水。

passages.en: While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was __(30)__ generations who paved the way, creating greater interest in Bath and its springs. Charles II, desperate for an heir and unable to produce a __(31)__ son, came to Bath to take the waters in the hope that their magical powers would do something to __(32)__ the situation. Craving for a male heir, James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son, which bred many conspiracy theories about who was the real father of their __(33)__ . Regardless, the 'miracle' created something of a boom in tourism for Bath and once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be, the whole nation __(34)__ to the city.
passages.zh: 乔治亚时代的人们使“饮用泉水”或泡浴变得尤为时髦，但正是更早的几代人为此铺平了道路，使人们对巴斯及其温泉产生了更大的兴趣。查理二世急于拥有一位继承人，却无法生育合法的儿子，于是来到巴斯饮用泉水，希望泉水的神奇力量能够设法改变这一状况。詹姆斯和玛丽渴望一位男性继承人，也一同来到巴斯，不久后便生下了一个儿子，这引发了许多关于谁才是他们后代真正父亲的阴谋论。无论如何，这一“奇迹”为巴斯的旅游业带来了某种程度的繁荣；1702年，安妮女王到访之后，巴斯成为人人向往的地方，全国民众纷纷涌入这座城市。

passages.en: Afterwards, the spas(矿泉疗养浴场) in Bath continued to go in and out of fashion for more than 150 years until they closed completely. The new Bath Spa, which opened in 2006, __(35)__ modern architecture with the ancient spring, now the New Royal Bath.
passages.zh: 此后，巴斯的矿泉疗养浴场时兴时衰了150多年，直到最终完全关闭。2006年开放的新巴斯温泉浴场将现代建筑与古老的泉水融为一体，如今称为新皇家浴场。

修饰形容词 pleasing 的副词
审美上令人愉悦 = 建筑美观 famous for its __ pleasing architecture 说的是巴斯以"美观的建筑"闻名，aesthetically pleasing 是英文里描述"赏心悦目、审美上令人愉快"的高频固定搭配，与后面"healing thermal springs"（治疗效果）并列，分别从美感和功效两方面定调全城特色。

K)principally义为"主要地"，与 pleasing 不搭 principally pleasing 意为"主要令人愉悦"，不符合英语习惯搭配；且 principally 通常修饰动词或限定范围（principally known as 等），更适合放在第 28 题修饰 known。 M)rhetorically修辞地 ≠ 美感 rhetorically 指"在修辞表达上"，与建筑外观的视觉美感没有关系，rhetorically pleasing architecture 在英语里不成立。
B) constructed动词
were ___ → 被动语态过去分词
建在泉水之上 upon which 引导的定语从句修饰 the King's Spring，意为"罗马浴场和神庙建在国王泉之上"，constructed（建造）正是该语义的标准词。
K) principally副词
修饰过去分词 known 的副词

"主要被认作罗马 & 乔治亚城"对应 although 让步 全句 Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city, many people came in the intervening centuries 用 although 让步："尽管巴斯主要以罗马 / 乔治亚之城闻名，但中间几个世纪也有很多人来"。principally"主要地"恰好建立"主流认知 vs. 例外史实"的对照，是该让步逻辑的标准副词。
M)rhetorically修辞地 known 不成立 rhetorically known 在英文中不成习惯搭配，且"修辞上被认作"与让步逻辑无关；本句讨论的是事实层面的主流印象，与修辞无关。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— rhetorically 词性也对、形态也对，唯独搭配不通。副词槽 Although Bath is __(28)__ known as a Roman and Georgian city 留下 principally 与 rhetorically 两词同时过关词性，词义又都比较"专业"，容易让考生选错。防坑：看 although 让步逻辑——只有"主要地"才能与让步对照（虽然主要是 A，但也有 B），rhetorically 没有让步含义。
H) natural形容词
the + 空 + 复数名词 waters → 修饰名词的形容词
natural waters = 天然温泉 上文 healing thermal springs 已点明巴斯的水是"天然温泉"，本句指"中间几个世纪人们来利用这些（天然温泉）水"，natural 直接呼应温泉的天然属性，搭配 natural waters 是英语描述天然泉水的常见说法。

G)legitimate"合法的水"语义荒谬 legitimate 指"合法的、婚生的"，与温泉水的属性毫不沾边；且 legitimate 在后文 unable to produce a __(31)__ son 里有更贴合的位置（legitimate son = 婚生子）。 O)versatile"多才多艺的水"不通 versatile 多形容人或物用途广，搭配 waters 不通顺；且全文没出现需要 versatile 的语境，它是典型的干扰词。
J) previous形容词
it was ___ generations who paved → 强调结构中修饰复数名词的形容词

previous generations 与下文乔治亚时代构成时间对照 本句让步逻辑是 While the Georgians made 'taking the waters' or bathing particularly fashionable, it was __(30)__ generations who paved the way——虽然是乔治亚人让"浴疗"流行起来，但真正铺路的是"前几代人"。previous generations"前几代人"正好与 the Georgians（乔治亚一代）形成时间上的对照，且与后文查理二世、詹姆士与玛丽这些"前任王朝"事例呼应。
O)versatile"多才多艺的几代人"与铺路逻辑无关 versatile generations 既不构成时间对照，也与"paved the way（铺路）"的因果关系无关；versatile 整篇都找不到落脚点，是命题人埋的干扰词。
G) legitimate形容词
a + 空 + 名词 son → 修饰 son 的形容词
legitimate son = 婚生子（合法继承人） 查理二世"desperate for an heir"——急需王位继承人；legitimate son 在英语里专指"婚生子"，即可以合法继承王位的儿子。下文 Craving for a male heir 再次印证关注点在合法男嗣，与 legitimate 完美吻合。
O)versatile多才多艺与王位继承无关 versatile son"多才多艺的儿子"与文意"急需合法继承人"完全错位；查理二世在意的不是儿子才艺，而是儿子是否婚生、是否能继位。
L) remedy动词
do something to + 动词原形 → 不定式动词

remedy the situation = 补救局面 查理二世来巴斯泡温泉 in the hope that their magical powers would do something to __ the situation，希望温泉魔力"做点什么来挽救 / 补救（生不出合法继承人的）局面"。remedy 作动词意为"纠正 / 补救"，remedy the situation 是英语固定搭配，与 desperate 的语气一致。
D)extract"提取局面"语义不通 extract 意为"提取 / 抽出"，搭配名词通常是 extract information/data/oil，不能与 situation 搭配；且与"求子续嗣"语境无关，是干扰项。
I) offspring名词
形容词性物主代词 their 后 → 名词
their offspring = 他们的子嗣 前文 James and Mary both came to Bath and soon after produced a son 明确他们生了一个儿子，本句又紧接"who was the real father of their __"，空处应是"他们的孩子"。offspring 正是"子女、后代"的中性书面词，与上下文阴谋论的语气吻合。
E) flocked动词
主语 the whole nation + 空 + to the city → 过去式动词

flock to = 蜂拥而至 前文铺垫"安妮女王 1702 年访问巴斯，把它坐实为时尚胜地"once Queen Anne had paid a visit in 1702, sealing it as the place to be，后面紧接"全国都___去这座城市"，逻辑上必须是"大规模、公开地涌向"，flocked（成群蜂拥而至）正是描写旅游热的标准词，与前句"created something of a boom in tourism"完美呼应。
N)sneaked潜行 ≠ 公开蜂拥 sneaked 指"偷偷溜走 / 潜行"，是小规模、隐秘的动作，主语是"全国（the whole nation）"时显然不合理；而且与"boom in tourism""the place to be"传递的高调、公开氛围正好相反，属典型反义诱惑项。

最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— sneaked 与 flocked 都能搭配 to，词义边界相反。the whole nation __(34)__ to the city 里 sneaked 看似也能填，是典型"正话反说"诱惑。防坑：看主语量级（the whole nation 是大规模、公开的）+ 上文气氛（boom in tourism、the place to be），明显与"偷偷溜走"矛盾。
F) incorporates动词
主语 The new Bath Spa + 空 → 第三人称单数动词
incorporate A with B = 把 A 与 B 融合 __(35)__ modern architecture with the ancient spring 的搭配框架"___ A with B"暗示"将现代建筑与古泉结合 / 融合"，incorporates"把……融合 / 并入"正是该框架的标准动词，与"new"（新）和"ancient"（古）形成的对比相呼应。
C)designatesdesignate = "指定 / 命名"，搭配 with 不成立 designate 通常搭配 as（designate A as B）或直接接宾语，不与 with 搭配；且语义"指定 / 命名"与"把现代建筑与古泉融合"完全不同，代入读不通。

longreading.title: 2022年6月·第1套 英语六级长篇阅读（信息匹配） 第 1 篇 · 36–45 题答案与解析

passages.en: A) Fazila is a young woman that has been dealing with eczema(湿疹), a common skin condition, for the past five years, but never got it treated. The nearest hospital is an hour away, by boat and bus, and her skin condition didn't seem serious enough to make the trek, so she ignored it—until a new technology brought the doctor to her. Fazila lives on one of the remote river islands in northern Bangladesh. These islands are low-lying, temporary sand islands that are continuously formed and destroyed through sand buildup and erosion. They are home to over six million people, who face repeated displacement from flooding and erosion—which may be getting worse because of climate change—and a range of health risks, including poor nutrition, malaria(疟疾) and other water-borne diseases.
passages.zh: 法齐拉是一名年轻女子，五年来一直受到湿疹这一常见皮肤病的困扰，却从未接受治疗。最近的医院需要乘船再转公交车，花一个小时才能到达，而她的皮肤状况似乎还没有严重到值得如此奔波，因此她一直没有理会，直到一项新技术把医生带到了她身边。法齐拉住在孟加拉国北部一座偏远的河流岛屿上。这些岛屿地势低洼，是由沙土堆积和侵蚀不断形成又不断消失的临时沙洲。岛上生活着六百多万人，他们因洪水和侵蚀而反复流离失所，而气候变化可能正在使这种情况恶化；他们还面临着一系列健康风险，包括营养不良、疟疾以及其他水传播疾病。

passages.en: B) The most dangerous thing for these remote island dwellers is land erosion. The second is lack of access to medical supplies and doctors. There are no doctors within miles, and while child mortality and maternal death have gone down in the rest of the country, this is not the case for the islands. The medical situation is so bad that it really takes away from the quality of their life. Yet for many island inhabitants—some of Bangladesh's poorest—paying for health care is a costly ordeal. Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers. Though government hospitals are free, many people hesitate to go, citing long commutes, endless lines and questionable diagnoses. For convenience's sake, one-third of rural households visit unqualified village doctors, who rely on unscientific methods of treatment, according to a 2016 study in the peer-reviewed journal Global Health Action.
passages.zh: 对于这些偏远岛屿的居民来说，最危险的事情是土地侵蚀。第二个问题是无法获得医疗用品和医生。方圆数英里内都没有医生；尽管该国其他地区的儿童死亡率和孕产妇死亡率都已下降，但岛上并非如此。岛上的医疗状况非常糟糕，严重影响了居民的生活质量。然而，对许多岛民来说——其中一些是孟加拉国最贫困的人——支付医疗费用是一件代价高昂的难事。土地侵蚀的受害者会失去房屋、农田以及作为农民、渔民和临时工的工作。虽然公立医院提供免费医疗，但许多人仍不愿前往，理由是路途遥远、排队无休无止以及诊断结果令人存疑。根据同行评议期刊《全球健康行动》2016年的一项研究，为了方便起见，三分之一的农村家庭会去找没有资质的乡村医生，而这些医生依靠不科学的方法进行治疗。

passages.en: C) On the islands, there's even a colloquial(口头的) expression for the idea of making medical care your lowest priority: It's known as "rog pushai rakha" in Bengali, which roughly translates to "stockpiling their diseases"—waiting to seek medical attention until a condition becomes extremely serious. Now, a new virtual medical service called Teledaktar (TD) is trying to make health care more easily accessible. Every week, TD's medical operators travel to the islands by boat, carrying a laptop, a portable printer for prescriptions and tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight. They choose an area of the island with the best Internet reception and set up a makeshift(临时凑合的) medical center which consists of plastic stools and small tables borrowed from the locals' homes, a tent in case of rain and a sheet that is strung up to give the patients privacy during their session.
passages.zh: 在这些岛屿上，人们甚至有一个口语表达，用来形容把医疗保健放在最低优先级的做法：孟加拉语称之为“rog pushai rakha”，大致可译为“囤积疾病”——也就是一直等到病情变得极其严重才寻求医疗救助。如今，一项名为Teledaktar（TD）的新型远程医疗服务正努力让医疗保健更容易获得。每周，TD的医疗工作人员都会乘船前往这些岛屿，携带一台笔记本电脑、一台用于打印处方的便携式打印机，以及进行基本医疗筛查的工具，如测量血压、血糖、体温和体重的设备。他们会选择岛上互联网信号最好的地方，搭建一个临时医疗中心。中心由从当地居民家中借来的塑料凳和小桌子组成；下雨时还会搭起帐篷，并悬挂一张床单，为患者就诊时提供隐私。

passages.en: D) Launched in October 2018, TD has eight centers in towns and villages across rural Bangladesh and on three islands. It is funded by a nonprofit organization founded by Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, finance and technology professionals. Inside the center, the laptop screen lights up to reveal Dr. Tina Mustahid, TD's head physician, live-streamed(网络直播) from the capital city of Dhaka for free remote medical consultations. Affectionately called Doctor Apa—"older sister" in Bengali—by her patients, she is one of three volunteer doctors at TD.
passages.zh: TD于2018年10月启动，目前在孟加拉国农村地区的城镇和村庄以及三座岛屿上设有八个中心。该项目由一个非营利组织资助，这个组织由孟加拉国的企业家、金融和技术专业人士创立。在中心内，笔记本电脑屏幕亮起，显示出TD首席医生蒂娜·穆斯塔希德医生的画面。她在首都达卡进行网络直播，为患者提供免费的远程医疗咨询。患者亲切地称她为“Doctor Apa”——在孟加拉语中意为“姐姐”；她是TD的三名志愿医生之一。

passages.en: E) "I diagnose them through conversation," says Dr. Mustahid. "Sometimes it's really obvious things that local doctors don't have the patience to talk through with their patients. For example, a common complaint mothers come in with is that their children refuse to eat their meals. The mothers are concerned they are dealing with indigestion, but it's because they are feeding the children packaged chips which are cheap and convenient. I tell them it is ruining their appetite and ask them to cut back on unhealthy snacks." Dr. Mustahid says building awareness about health and nutrition is important for island patients who are cut off from mainland resources.
passages.zh: 穆斯塔希德医生说：“我是通过交谈来诊断他们的。有时，事情其实非常明显，只是当地医生没有耐心和患者仔细沟通。例如，母亲们来就诊时常见的一个抱怨是，她们的孩子拒绝吃饭。母亲们担心孩子消化不良，但实际上是因为她们给孩子吃了包装薯片，这种食物既便宜又方便。我告诉她们，这会破坏孩子的食欲，并让她们减少不健康零食的摄入。”穆斯塔希德医生说，对于与大陆资源隔绝的岛上患者而言，提高健康和营养意识十分重要。

passages.en: F) Even off the islands, Bangladesh faces a critical deficit of health services. The country has half the doctors-per-person ratio recommended by the World Health Organization: roughly one doctor per 2,000 people, instead of one doctor per 1,000 people. And of those physicians, many are concentrated in cities: 70% of the country's population live in rural areas, yet less than 20% of health workers practice there. Over 70% of TD's 3,000 patients are female, in part because many are not comfortable speaking with local doctors who tend to be male. The rural women are mostly not literate or confident enough to travel on their own to the nearest town to visit medical facilities. Many have spent their entire lives rebuilding their homes when the islands flood. Early marriage and young motherhood, which are prevalent in these parts of Bangladesh, also contribute to the early onset of health problems.
passages.zh: 即使离开这些岛屿，孟加拉国仍面临医疗服务严重不足的问题。该国每千人的医生数量只有世界卫生组织建议水平的一半左右：大约每2,000人拥有一名医生，而不是每1,000人拥有一名医生。在这些医生中，许多人集中在城市：该国有70%的人口生活在农村地区，但在那里执业的卫生工作者不到20%。TD的3,000名患者中，超过70%是女性，部分原因是许多女性不习惯与通常为男性的当地医生交谈。农村妇女大多不识字，也缺乏独自前往最近城镇就医的能力或信心。许多人一生都在岛屿遭遇洪水时重建自己的家园。孟加拉国这些地区普遍存在的早婚和年轻母亲现象，也促成了健康问题的早期出现。

passages.en: G) For most TD patients on the islands, Dr. Mustahid is the first big-city doctor that they've ever consulted. TD doctors are not meant to treat serious illnesses or conditions that require a doctor to be physically present, such as pregnancy. But they can write prescriptions, diagnose common ailments—including digestive issues, joint pain, skin diseases, fever and the common cold—and refer patients to doctors at local hospitals. The visit is also an opportunity for the patients, especially women, to air their concerns about aging, motherhood and reproductive health according to Dr. Mustahid. The doctors also offer health, dietary and lifestyle advice where necessary, including insight on everything from recognizing postnatal(产后的) depression to daily exercise. Dr. Mustahid regularly recommends her patients to take a daily thirty-minute morning walk before the sun gets too intense.
passages.zh: 对于岛上大多数TD患者来说，穆斯塔希德医生是她们一生中咨询过的第一位大城市医生。TD的医生并不负责治疗重病，也不负责处理需要医生亲自到场的情况，例如妊娠。但他们可以开具处方，诊断常见疾病，包括消化问题、关节疼痛、皮肤病、发烧和普通感冒，并将患者转诊给当地医院的医生。穆斯塔希德医生说，就诊也是患者，尤其是女性，倾诉自己对衰老、母亲身份和生殖健康方面担忧的机会。必要时，医生还会提供健康、饮食和生活方式方面的建议，内容包括如何识别产后抑郁以及进行日常锻炼等各个方面。穆斯塔希德医生经常建议患者每天早晨步行30分钟，时间要赶在太阳变得过于强烈之前。

passages.en: H) After a few sessions about general health issues Fazila finally opened up about something else that was bothering her: her persistent skin condition. It can get expensive to travel to the doctor, so usually the women living on the islands describe their illness to their husbands. The husbands then go to the pharmacy, try to describe the issue and return home with some random medicines. Nothing worked for Fazila until she started seeing Dr. Apa.
passages.zh: 在接受了几次关于一般健康问题的咨询后，法齐拉终于说出了另一件困扰她的事：她那持续不愈的皮肤病。去看医生可能需要花费很多钱，因此，通常住在岛上的妇女会把自己的病情告诉丈夫。丈夫们随后前往药店，试着描述病情，然后带着一些随意购买的药物回家。在开始接受Doctor Apa的诊治之前，法齐拉尝试的药物没有一种有效。

passages.en: I) Other nonprofits are also starting to provide health services on the islands. A local non-governmental organization called Friendship operates floating boat hospitals that provide health services to islands all over Bangladesh, docking at each for two months at a time. Friendship also runs satellite clinics in which one doctor and one clinic aide who are residents of the community disperse health and hygiene information.
passages.zh: 其他非营利组织也开始在这些岛屿上提供医疗服务。当地一家名为Friendship的非政府组织运营着漂浮的船上医院，为孟加拉国各地的岛屿提供医疗服务，每次在一个岛上停留两个月。Friendship还运营着卫星诊所，由一名医生和一名身为当地居民的诊所助理负责传播健康与卫生信息。

passages.en: J) TD still has a few major challenges. Many residents complain the medicines they are prescribed are sometimes unaffordable, but the government isn't doing enough for them. Patients often ask why the medicine isn't free along with the consultation from the doctors. The organizations are linked to local pharmacies and offer discounts to the patients and make sure to prescribe the most cost-effective brands, but still many residents can't afford even that.
passages.zh: TD仍面临几个重大挑战。许多居民抱怨说，给他们开的药有时负担不起，但政府为他们所做的还不够。患者经常问，为什么医生的咨询是免费的，药物却不能一并免费提供。这些组织与当地药店建立了联系，为患者提供折扣，并确保开出最具性价比的品牌，但许多居民仍然连折后价格也负担不起。

passages.en: K) Nevertheless, TD's remote consultations seem to be popular: Of 3,000 patients, at least 200 have returned for follow-ups, according to TD. The reason, explains one resident, might be the simple gesture of treating the island inhabitants with respect. "Dr. Apa is patient," he says, "At government hospitals, the doctors treat us very badly, but here they listen to us, I can repeat myself many times and no one gets annoyed."
passages.zh: 尽管如此，TD的远程医疗咨询似乎很受欢迎：TD称，在3,000名患者中，至少有200人回来复诊。一位居民解释说，原因可能在于他们以一种简单的举动给予岛民尊重。他说：“Doctor Apa很有耐心。在公立医院，医生对我们非常差劲，但在这里，他们会听我们说话；我可以重复很多遍，也没有人会感到厌烦。”

statements.en: Some children on the remote islands won't eat their meals because they are fed cheap junk food.
statements.zh: 偏远岛屿上的一些儿童不愿意吃饭,因为他们被喂食廉价的垃圾食品。

analysis.锚点: 孩子不肯吃饭+垃圾零食
analysis.定位: E 段 The mothers are concerned they are dealing with indigestion, but it's because they are feeding the children packaged chips which are cheap and convenient. 母亲们担心孩子是消化不良，但其实是因为她们给孩子吃了既便宜又方便的袋装薯片。
analysis.改写: children↔their children 同词复现 won't eat their meals↔refuse to eat their meals 助动词否定替换实义动词 cheap junk food↔packaged chips which are cheap and convenient 上位词概括下位实例

statements.en: Unlike other parts of Bangladesh, the number of women who die from giving birth remains high on the river islands.
statements.zh: 与孟加拉国其他地区不同,河中岛屿上因分娩而死亡的妇女人数仍然很高。

analysis.锚点: 孕产妇死亡率+岛屿例外
analysis.定位: B 段 There are no doctors within miles, and while child mortality and maternal death have gone down in the rest of the country, this is not the case for the islands. 周围几英里内都没有医生，而虽然儿童死亡率与孕产妇死亡率在该国其他地方都下降了，岛上却并非如此。
analysis.改写: women who die from giving birth↔maternal death 术语口语化解释 Unlike other parts of Bangladesh↔while ... have gone down in the rest of the country 让步连词替换 remains high on the river islands↔this is not the case for the islands 否定下降即维持高位
analysis.辨邻: F F 段虽然 Over 70% of TD's 3,000 patients are female 都涉及女性，但话题是女性占患者比例与早婚早育，没有讨论 women who die from giving birth 这一死亡率话题，因此不是源头段。 Over 70% of TD's 3,000 patients are female

statements.en: One big problem many islanders have is that they can't afford the prescribed medicines, even with discounts offered.
statements.zh: 许多岛民面临的一个大问题是,即使有折扣优惠,他们也负担不起处方药。

analysis.锚点: 买不起处方药+有折扣仍贵
analysis.定位: J 段 The organizations are linked to local pharmacies and offer discounts to the patients and make sure to prescribe the most cost-effective brands, but still many residents can't afford even that. 这些组织已经对接了当地药店、给患者提供折扣、并尽量开最具性价比的品牌，但仍有许多居民连这样的价格都负担不起。
analysis.改写: can't afford the prescribed medicines↔the medicines they are prescribed are sometimes unaffordable 形容词转动词短语 even with discounts offered↔offer discounts to the patients 并列让步压缩成介词短语

statements.en: TD is a virtual medical service financially supported by one of the nation's nonprofit organizations.
statements.zh: TD是一项由国家非营利组织之一提供资金支持的虚拟医疗服务。

analysis.锚点: TD 由非营利组织资助
analysis.定位: D 段 It is funded by a nonprofit organization founded by Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, finance and technology professionals. 它由一家由孟加拉企业家、金融与科技专业人士创办的非营利组织资助。
analysis.改写: virtual medical service↔Dr. Tina Mustahid ... live-streamed ... for free remote medical consultations 概括上位词复述服务形态 financially supported by one of the nation's nonprofit organizations↔funded by a nonprofit organization founded by Bangladeshi entrepreneurs, finance and technology professionals funded = financially supported；the nation's = Bangladeshi
analysis.辨邻: C C 段虽然 Now, a new virtual medical service called Teledaktar (TD) 首次正式介绍了 TD 是虚拟医疗服务，但只描述了 TD 每周登岛、设临时医疗点的运作方式，没有说 TD 由谁资助，因此无法承载题干关于资金来源的具体陈述。 a new virtual medical service called Teledaktar (TD) is trying to make health care more easily accessible

statements.en: TD doctors are welcome to the islanders because they treat the sick with respect and patience.
statements.zh: TD的医生受到岛民欢迎,因为他们以尊重和耐心的态度治疗病人。

analysis.定位: K 段 The reason, explains one resident, might be the simple gesture of treating the island inhabitants with respect. "Dr. Apa is patient," he says, "At government hospitals, the doctors treat us very badly, but here they listen to us, I can repeat myself many times and no one gets annoyed." 一位居民解释说，原因可能就在于他们以尊重的姿态对待岛民这一简单的举动。他说：Doctor Apa 很有耐心；在公立医院里医生对我们态度很差，但在这里他们会听我们说话，我可以反复说很多遍也没人觉得烦。
analysis.改写: welcome to the islanders↔TD's remote consultations seem to be popular 受欢迎 = popular treat the sick with respect↔treating the island inhabitants with respect 同结构 + 同词复现 patience↔Dr. Apa is patient 形容词↔名词

statements.en: Women islanders tend to have health problems early partly because they get married and give birth early.
statements.zh: 女性岛民往往较早出现健康问题,部分原因是她们结婚和生育都较早。

analysis.锚点: 早婚早育→健康问题提前
analysis.定位: F 段 Early marriage and young motherhood, which are prevalent in these parts of Bangladesh, also contribute to the early onset of health problems. 在孟加拉这些地区相当普遍的早婚与年轻就当母亲，也促成了健康问题的提前出现。
analysis.改写: get married and give birth early↔Early marriage and young motherhood 名词短语↔动词短语 have health problems early↔the early onset of health problems 名词化结果同义 partly because↔also contribute to 部分原因的两种表达

statements.en: TD doctors make weekly visits to the remote islands to provide services at a temporary medical center.
statements.zh: TD的医生每周访问偏远岛屿,在临时医疗中心提供服务。

analysis.定位: C 段 Every week, TD's medical operators travel to the islands by boat, carrying a laptop, a portable printer for prescriptions and tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight. They choose an area of the island with the best Internet reception and set up a makeshift medical center which consists of plastic stools and small tables borrowed from the locals' homes, a tent in case of rain and a sheet that is strung up to give the patients privacy during their session. 每周 TD 的医务人员都会乘船前往岛屿，随身带着笔记本电脑、用于打印处方的便携打印机，以及测血压、血糖、体温与体重等基础筛查的工具。他们会挑岛上信号最好的地方，借居民家的塑料凳子与小桌子搭起一个临时医疗点，下雨时再搭起一顶帐篷，并拉一块布单为患者提供问诊隐私。
analysis.改写: weekly visits↔Every week, TD's medical operators travel to the islands by boat 频率短语 ↔ 形容词 a temporary medical center↔a makeshift medical center 同义形容词替换

statements.en: TD doctors provide the islanders with online diagnoses and treatments for common diseases.
statements.zh: TD的医生为岛民提供常见疾病的在线诊断和治疗。

analysis.定位: G 段 But they can write prescriptions, diagnose common ailments—including digestive issues, joint pain, skin diseases, fever and the common cold—and refer patients to doctors at local hospitals. 但他们可以开处方、诊断包括消化问题、关节疼痛、皮肤病、发烧、普通感冒在内的常见小病，并把患者转诊给当地医院的医生。
analysis.改写: online diagnoses and treatments↔write prescriptions, diagnose common ailments 开处方+诊断 = 诊治；online 隐含 common diseases↔common ailments—including digestive issues, joint pain, skin diseases, fever and the common cold 上位词 + 下位实例列举
analysis.辨邻: E E 段虽然 I diagnose them through conversation 也提到诊断，但讲的是一次具体的母亲带孩子来看消化问题的案例，并没有列出 TD 能诊治哪些常见病的总体定性，因此不是题干 common diseases 这一概括陈述的源头段。 I diagnose them through conversation C C 段 tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight 只讲基础筛查项目，并没有给出 TD 诊治哪些 common diseases 的清单，因此不是题干 common diseases 的源头段。 tools to run basic medical screenings such as blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature and weight

statements.en: The residents of the river islands have to keep moving their homes because of floods and land erosions.
statements.zh: 河中岛屿的居民由于洪水和土地侵蚀而不得不不断搬迁家园。

analysis.定位: A 段 They are home to over six million people, who face repeated displacement from flooding and erosion—which may be getting worse because of climate change—and a range of health risks, including poor nutrition, malaria and other water-borne diseases. 这些岛屿是六百多万人的家园，他们因洪水与侵蚀而反复被迫迁居——这种情况可能因气候变化而变得更糟——还要面对营养不良、疟疾以及其他水媒疾病等一系列健康风险。
analysis.改写: keep moving their homes↔repeated displacement 名词化 ↔ 动词化 floods and land erosions↔flooding and erosion 同根名词改复数
analysis.辨邻: B B 段 Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers 讲的是侵蚀让人失去房屋、土地与工作，没有强调反复迁居这一动作，因此不是题干 keep moving their homes 的源头段。 Victims of erosion lose their houses, agricultural land and jobs as farmers, fishermen and day laborers

statements.en: Women islanders usually rely on their husbands to get some medicines for them without diagnoses and prescriptions.
statements.zh: 女性岛民通常依靠丈夫在没有诊断和处方的情况下为她们买一些药物。

analysis.锚点: 丈夫代买药+无诊断处方
analysis.定位: H 段 It can get expensive to travel to the doctor, so usually the women living on the islands describe their illness to their husbands. The husbands then go to the pharmacy, try to describe the issue and return home with some random medicines. 去看医生开销很大，所以岛上的女性平时只能把自己的病情描述给丈夫；丈夫再到药店去，尽量把病情转述一遍，然后带一些随机的药回家。
analysis.改写: rely on their husbands to get some medicines↔The husbands then go to the pharmacy, try to describe the issue and return home with some random medicines 动作链压缩成一句动宾 without diagnoses and prescriptions↔describe their illness to their husbands 流程中无医生介入即无诊断与处方
analysis.辨邻: B B 段 one-third of rural households visit unqualified village doctors 描述的是去找未受训的村医，没有出现丈夫代女买药这一具体行为，因此不是题干 Q45 的源头段。 one-third of rural households visit unqualified village doctors

reading1.title: 2022年6月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 1 篇 · 46–50 题答案与解析

passages.en: Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive, and for not training graduates for the world of work. Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.
passages.zh: 美国的高选择性学院和大学因过于精英化、学费过于昂贵，以及没有为毕业生进入职场做好培训而受到抨击。这些指责忽视了这样一个事实：这些学校仍在继续帮助学生为事业上的成功、对公民生活的理性参与、终身学习，以及理解他们所处的世界和与他们共同生活的人做好准备。

passages.en: These colleges and universities must be doing something right. Applications are at record highs, and their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever. This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.
passages.zh: 这些学院和大学一定做对了什么。申请人数创下历史新高，而它们的助学金项目使其比以往任何时候都更容易进入。这种教育模式长期以来一直在创造机会、推动经济增长和促进创新方面发挥着核心作用。

passages.en: Yet, there is growing skepticism about the value of this model. The recent tax reform bill is a wake-up call that our strongest colleges and universities are under assault by some in government. The initial proposals would have made education unaffordable for many by taxing tuition waivers for graduate students and ending deductions for student loan interest. Thankfully, these provisions were ultimately stripped from the bill, but lawmakers let stand a new tax on the investment income of some colleges and universities.
passages.zh: 然而，人们对这种模式的价值日益持怀疑态度。最近的税制改革法案敲响了警钟，表明我们最优秀的学院和大学正受到政府中一些人的攻击。最初的提案会通过对研究生的学费减免征税以及取消学生贷款利息抵扣，使许多人无力承担教育费用。所幸，这些条款最终被从法案中删除，但立法者却保留了针对部分学院和大学投资收入的新税。

passages.en: While these attacks are motivated by misguided ideas, we need to do a better job of explaining why these claims are false and why what we do is valuable. We cannot take for granted that any of this is obvious.
passages.zh: 尽管这些攻击源于错误的观念，但我们需要更好地解释为什么这些说法是错误的，以及我们所做的事情为何具有价值。我们不能想当然地认为这些道理都是显而易见的。

passages.en: It is often said that elite colleges and universities do not train students, particularly those who study the liberal arts, for the workforce. But this can be refuted by scholarly research. The data are clear: a liberal arts education is great career preparation, both for excellent lifetime earnings and for satisfaction with the work. This education develops the skills of critical thinking, rigorous analysis of data and facts, communication with the written and spoken word, understanding of cultural differences and issues, and the ability to keep learning. In fact, liberal arts graduates do extremely well in every imaginable field.
passages.zh: 人们常说，精英学院和大学没有为学生，尤其是学习文科的学生，进入职场做好培训。但学术研究可以驳斥这一说法。数据十分明确：文科教育是极好的职业准备，既能带来优厚的终身收入，也能提高对工作的满意度。这种教育培养批判性思维能力、对数据和事实进行严谨分析的能力、通过书面和口头语言进行交流的能力、理解文化差异和相关问题的能力，以及持续学习的能力。事实上，文科毕业生在所有可以想象的领域都表现得非常出色。

passages.en: Access to an education at selective colleges and universities is now more available than ever to low- and middle-income families. We have built endowments from donations by alumni(校友) and parents who understand and appreciate our mission to provide access and opportunity, and a significant portion of the returns from these endowments is used to fund financial aid.
passages.zh: 如今，低收入和中等收入家庭比以往任何时候都更有机会接受高选择性学院和大学的教育。我们依靠校友和家长的捐赠建立了捐赠基金；他们理解并认可我们提供机会和入学机会的使命，而这些捐赠基金的投资回报中有相当大一部分被用于资助助学金。

passages.en: Ironically, the new tax on endowments drains financial aid funds from the very schools most able to offer opportunity to those who have earned a spot but cannot otherwise afford this education. Beyond the virtue of access to those who have earned a place at these schools, the diversity of economic backgrounds enhances the education and experience of all of our students.
passages.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，这项针对捐赠基金的新税削减了那些最有能力为有资格入学却无力承担这种教育费用的人提供机会的学校的助学金资金。除了让那些凭自身努力获得这些学校入学资格的人能够接受教育这一优点之外，不同经济背景的多样性也提升了我们所有学生所接受的教育及其经历。

questions.stem: What fact does the author emphasize concerning selective colleges and universities?
questions.stem_zh: 关于选择性学院和大学,作者强调了什么事实?

options.text: They have been ignoring the training of graduates for the world of work.
options.zh: 它们一直忽视对毕业生进入职场的培训。

options.text: They have been doing well in ensuring their students a successful future.
options.zh: 它们一直在确保学生拥有成功未来方面做得很好。

options.text: They have been constantly attacked for being too elite and too expensive.
options.zh: 它们一直因过于精英化和过于昂贵而不断受到抨击。

options.text: They have been actively engaged in civic life beyond the school campus.
options.zh: 它们一直积极参与校园之外的公民生活。

questions.判型: What fact does the author emphasize 明确询问作者强调的事实，对应原文某一处具体表述，不要求跨段推断。
questions.拆句: 主干是 What fact does the author emphasize，concerning selective colleges and universities 是介词短语后置修饰 fact，相当于 about。无否定、无比较，平铺直叙。
questions.定位: P1 Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live. 这些指控忽视了一个事实：这些院校仍在持续地为学生做准备——为他们的事业成功、公民生活的深入参与、终身学习，以及理解世界与共处之人做准备。

locate.en: Such charges ignore the fact that these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work, for thoughtful engagement in civic life, for lifelong learning, and for understanding the world and those with whom they live.
locate.zh: 这些指控忽视了一个事实：这些院校仍在持续地为学生做准备——为他们的事业成功、公民生活的深入参与、终身学习，以及理解世界与共处之人做准备。

option_analysis.note: They have been ignoring the training of graduates for the world of work 把“忽视”这一动作扣到了院校头上，正好与原文相反——原文是说指控者忽视了事实，并不是院校忽视培养。
预判说“院校仍在为学生未来成功做准备”，B 项 doing well in ensuring their students a successful future 正是这一表述的同义替换，故选 B。

pairs.orig: these institutions continue to prepare students for success in their work
pairs.opt: doing well in ensuring their students a successful future

pairs.orig: Such charges ignore the fact that
pairs.opt: They have been doing well

option_analysis.note: They have been constantly attacked for being too elite and too expensive 复述的是 Selective colleges and universities in the U.S. are under fire for being too elite and too expensive 这一事实——但这是别人对院校的指控，不是作者要强调的 fact；题干问 What fact does the author emphasize。
They have been actively engaged in civic life beyond the school campus 把原文中“院校培养学生参与公民生活”的对象（学生）偷换成了院校本身参与公民生活，主体被替换。

questions.stem: What does the author say in arguing for the model of education in the U.S.?
questions.stem_zh: 作者在论证美国教育模式时说了什么?

options.text: It has contributed substantially to the nation's overall development.
options.zh: 它对国家的整体发展做出了重大贡献。

options.text: It has succeeded in maintaining sustainable financial aid programs.
options.zh: 它成功维持了可持续的财政资助项目。

options.text: It has given priority to innovative programs for graduate studies.
options.zh: 它优先考虑研究生学习的创新项目。

options.text: It has played a central role in attracting international applicants.
options.zh: 它在吸引国际申请者方面发挥了核心作用。

questions.判型: What does the author say 询问作者具体表态了什么，对应一句具体陈述，仍属细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What does the author say，in arguing for the model of education in the U.S. 是介词短语作状语，交代 say 发生的语境。结构简单。
questions.定位: P2 This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation. 这一教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长与激发创新方面扮演着核心角色。

locate.en: This model of education has long played a central role in creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation.
locate.zh: 这一教育模式长期以来在创造机会、推动经济增长与激发创新方面扮演着核心角色。

option_analysis.note: 三项并列贡献可统一抽象为 the nation's overall development，A 项正是这一上位概括，故选 A。

pairs.orig: creating opportunity, driving economic growth, and spurring innovation
pairs.opt: contributed substantially to the nation's overall development

pairs.orig: has long played a central role
pairs.opt: contributed substantially

option_analysis.note: succeeded in maintaining sustainable financial aid programs 把“该模式的整体贡献”偷换成了“维持可持续的资助项目”——原文 their financial aid programs make them more accessible than ever 只是说援助项目使学校更可及，没说“可持续维持”，更不是作者为之辩护的核心论据。
given priority to innovative programs for graduate studies 把 spurring innovation 中的 innovation 拼接成“研究生项目优先”，但原文从未谈及研究生项目优先级，是凭空捏造。
played a central role in attracting international applicants 套用了原文 played a central role 的句式，却把宾语换成了 attracting international applicants（吸引国际申请人），但原文从未提国际申请人，是用熟悉句式包装的新内容。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the initial proposals concerning the recent tax reform bill?
questions.stem_zh: 关于近期税改法案的初步提案,我们了解到什么?

options.text: They would have stripped many students of life's chances.
options.zh: 它们本会剥夺许多学生的人生机会。

options.text: They would have deducted graduate student loan interest.
options.zh: 它们本会扣除研究生学生贷款利息。

options.text: They would have added to many students' financial burden.
options.zh: 它们本会增加许多学生的经济负担。

options.text: They would have increased the number of tuition waivers.
options.zh: 它们本会增加学费减免的数量。

questions.判型: What do we learn about the initial proposals 问关于某物的具体信息，定位句即答案出处，属细节题。
questions.拆句: 主干 What do we learn about the initial proposals，concerning the recent tax reform bill 是 the initial proposals 的后置修饰。注意虚拟语气 would have made 暗示这些提议未实施，比对选项时四个选项都是 would have，与原文虚拟一致。

reading2.title: 2022年6月·第1套 英语六级阅读理解（四选一） 第 2 篇 · 51–55 题答案与解析

passages.en: When a group of Australians was asked why they believed climate change was not happening, about 36% said it was "common sense", according to a report published last year by the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization. This was the most popular reason for their opinion, with only 11% saying their belief that climate change was not happening was based on scientific research.
passages.zh: 根据澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织去年发布的一份报告，当被问及为什么相信气候变化并未发生时，约36%的澳大利亚人回答说这是“常识”。这是他们持有这一观点的最普遍理由，只有11%的人表示，他们认为气候变化并未发生的信念是基于科学研究的。

passages.en: But what do we mean by an appeal to common sense? Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning. The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. Whether it feels right is usually a reflection of the world view and ideologies we have internalised, and that frames how we interact with new ideas. When new ideas are in accord with what we already believe, they are more readily accepted. When they are not, they, and the arguments that lead to them, are more readily rejected.
passages.zh: 但是，我们所说的诉诸常识究竟是什么意思？想必它是诉诸某种理性，而这种理性构成了更复杂推理的基础。然而，诉诸常识通常不过是诉诸一种让人感觉正确的思考方式，但对一个人来说感觉正确的事情，对另一个人来说未必如此。事情是否感觉正确，通常反映了我们内化的世界观和意识形态，而它们决定了我们如何与新观念互动。当新观念与我们原有的信念相一致时，我们更容易接受它们；当它们不一致时，我们则更容易拒绝这些观念以及导向它们的论证。

passages.en: We often mistake this automatic compatibility testing of new ideas with existing beliefs as an application of common sense, but, in reality, it is more about judging than thinking. As Nobelist Daniel Kahneman notes in Thinking, Fast and Slow, when we arrive at conclusions in this way, the outcomes also feel true, regardless of whether they are. We are not psychologically well equipped to judge our own thinking.
passages.zh: 我们常常把这种将新观念与现有信念进行自动兼容性检验的过程误认为是在运用常识，但实际上，这更多的是在评判，而不是在思考。正如诺贝尔奖得主丹尼尔·卡尼曼在《思考，快与慢》中所指出的，当我们以这种方式得出结论时，无论结论是否正确，结果都会让人感觉真实。我们在心理上并不具备充分评判自己思维的能力。

passages.en: We are also highly susceptible to a range of cognitive biases such as giving preference to the first things that come to mind when making decisions or giving weight to evidence.
passages.zh: 我们还很容易受到各种认知偏差的影响，例如在作出决定或评估证据时，偏爱最先想到的事情，或赋予某些证据更大的分量。

passages.en: One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science.
passages.zh: 检验我们的内在偏见和不一致之处的一种方法，是通过知识的社会验证来进行检验，在这一过程中，我们以严谨且系统的方式检验自己的观念，看看它们是否不仅对我们自己说得通，对其他人是否也说得通。这种社会共享认知的杰出范例就是科学。

passages.en: That does not mean that individuals are not capable of excellent thinking, nor does it mean no individual is rational. But the extent to which individuals can do this on their own is a function of how well integrated they are with communities of systematic inquiry in the first place. You can't learn to think well by yourself.
passages.zh: 这并不意味着个人没有能力进行出色的思考，也不意味着没有任何个人是理性的。但个人能够独自做到这一点的程度，取决于他们起初与系统探究共同体的融合程度。你无法独自学会良好地思考。

passages.en: In matters of science at least, those who value their common sense over methodological, collaborative investigation imagine themselves to be more free in their thinking, unbound by involvement with the group, but in reality they are tightly bound by their capabilities and perspectives. We are smarter together than we are individually, and perhaps that's just common sense.
passages.zh: 至少在科学问题上，那些把常识置于有方法的协作性调查之上的人，以为自己在思考时更加自由，不受参与群体的束缚，但实际上，他们受到自身能力和视角的严格限制。我们共同思考时比各自单独思考时更加聪明，而这或许就是常识。

questions.stem: What is the appeal to common sense according to the author?
questions.stem_zh: 根据作者的观点,诉诸常识是什么?

options.text: It is the basis for the internalisation of individuals' ideologies.
options.zh: 它是个体意识形态内化的基础。

options.text: It is a series of conceptions formulated from complex reasoning.
options.zh: 它是一系列通过复杂推理形成的概念。

options.text: It is collective wisdom that helps people interact with new ideas.
options.zh: 它是帮助人们与新观念互动的集体智慧。

options.text: It is something subjective based on what one perceives to be right.
options.zh: 它是基于个人对正确事物的认知的主观性内容。

questions.判型: What is the appeal to common sense according to the author 直接问一个概念"是什么"，定义在文中可被直接定位回答。
questions.拆句: Q52 主干 "What is the appeal to common sense"，according to the author 是介词短语作整句的状语，限定信息来源；句式简单。
questions.定位: P2 The appeal to common sense, however, is usually nothing more than an appeal to thinking that just feels right, but what feels right to one person may not feel right to another. locate.zh: 然而所谓"诉诸常识"，往往不过是诉诸"感觉对"的想法罢了，可一个人觉得对，另一个人未必觉得对。是否觉得对，通常只是我们已经内化的世界观和意识形态的投射。

原文 Presumably it's an appeal to rationality of some sort that forms the basis of more complex reasoning 是作者先假设的"理想状态"，紧随 however, is usually nothing more than 被否定；formulated from complex reasoning 恰是被否定的那一面。

locate.en: One way we can check our internal biases and inconsistencies is through the social verification of knowledge, in which we test our ideas in a rigorous and systematic way to see if they make sense not just to us, but to other people. The outstanding example of this socially shared cognition is science.
locate.zh: 我们能够检验自身内在偏差与矛盾的一种方式，是通过对知识的社会化检验：以严格、系统的方式检验我们的想法，看它们不仅对自己说得通，对别人也是否说得通。这种社会共享认知最杰出的例子就是科学。

option_analysis.note: P4 只提到我们对证据有偏向，Give equal weight to evidence of both sides in a conflict 把它包装成"双方等量赋权"作为对策；原文从未给出这一对策。
原文谈"用科学的社会共享认知去检验自己的想法"，并未提及在论证中 Provide convincing examples in developing an argument"举有说服力的例子"这一具体写作技巧。
预判"通过社会化检验、典型即科学"与 Establish socially shared cognition via scientific methods 在两个核心点上同义对齐——前半部分是手段，后半部分是手段的载体。

translation.title: 2022年6月·第1套英语六级汉译英（段落翻译） · 客观介绍卢沟桥的历史与石刻艺术 参考译文与解析
translation.directions: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to translate a passage from Chinese into English. You should write your answer on Answer Sheet 2.
translation.source_zh: 卢沟桥位于天安门广场西南15公里处，横跨永定河，是北京现存最古老的多拱石桥。卢沟桥最初建成于1192年，1698年重建，由281根柱子支撑。每根柱子上都有一头石狮。这些石狮的头、背、腹部或爪子上都藏着更多的狮子。这些石狮生动逼真、千姿百态，是卢沟桥石刻艺术的精品。桥上的石狮不计其数，因而北京地区流传着"卢沟桥上的石狮子——数不清"的说法。 卢沟桥不仅以其美学特征闻名于世，还被公认为石桥建筑史上的一座丰碑。
translation.reference_en:
Located 15 kilometres southwest of Tian'anmen Square and spanning the Yongding River, Lugou Bridge is the oldest existing multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing. It was first built in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698, and is supported by 281 pillars. On each pillar stands a stone lion, and on the heads, backs, bellies or paws of these stone lions are hidden even more lions. Vivid and lifelike and varying in posture, these stone lions are regarded as the finest works of stone carving on Lugou Bridge. The stone lions on the bridge are too numerous to count, so there is a popular saying in the Beijing area: "The stone lions on Lugou Bridge are simply countless." Lugou Bridge is not only world-famous for its aesthetic features but also widely recognized as a monument in the history of stone bridge construction.
【衔接】
第1句与第2句之间：用 It 承接避免重复桥名第1句主语已是 Lugou Bridge，第2句 卢沟桥最初建成于1192年 中文又重复「卢沟桥」。英文若再写一遍 Lugou Bridge 显啰嗦，改用代词 It 承接：It was first built in 1192…，读起来连贯不重复。
第3句与第4句之间：用 some 之类显出「更多」的层次第3句说每柱一狮，第4句 都藏着更多的狮子 是在前句基础上的递进（大狮身上还藏小狮）。英文可在第4句用 even more lions/still more lions 的 even/still 强调这层「在已有基础上更多」，让两句的递进关系显出来。
第5句与第6句之间：信息顺承，无需强加连词第5句讲石狮的艺术价值，第6句 桥上的石狮不计其数 转入数量之多并引出谚语，话题自然顺承，保持各自独立成句即可，不必硬加 moreover 一类连词。

cohesion.core: 第1句与第2句之间：用 It 承接避免重复桥名
cohesion.detail: 第1句主语已是 Lugou Bridge，第2句 卢沟桥最初建成于1192年 中文又重复「卢沟桥」。英文若再写一遍 Lugou Bridge 显啰嗦，改用代词 It 承接：It was first built in 1192…，读起来连贯不重复。

cohesion.core: 第3句与第4句之间：用 some 之类显出「更多」的层次
cohesion.detail: 第3句说每柱一狮，第4句 都藏着更多的狮子 是在前句基础上的递进（大狮身上还藏小狮）。英文可在第4句用 even more lions/still more lions 的 even/still 强调这层「在已有基础上更多」，让两句的递进关系显出来。

main_idea.core: 客观介绍卢沟桥的历史与石刻艺术
main_idea.detail: 全篇是对中国一处历史名胜的客观介绍：先讲它的位置与地位 是北京现存最古老的多拱石桥，再讲它的石狮与艺术价值，最后讲它的地位定评 被公认为石桥建筑史上的一座丰碑。属四六级最常见的「中国文化/名胜介绍」语体——陈述客观事实、不带个人情绪，用词偏书面、客观。

tense.detail: 全篇主体在陈述卢沟桥「现在仍然如此」的客观事实——它的位置 卢沟桥位于天安门广场西南15公里处、它现存的地位 是北京现存最古老的多拱石桥、桥上石狮的样貌与价值，这些都是当下成立的常态，故以一般现在时为主。只有讲到历史上「建成/重建」这种已完成的过去动作时，才偏离基调改用一般过去时。

term_notes.detail: 采用约定俗成的官方译名 Lugou Bridge（也作 Marco Polo Bridge，但考场首选拼音译名 Lugou Bridge 最稳）。全篇 卢沟桥 反复出现，必须前后只用这一种译法，不要一会儿 Lugou Bridge 一会儿 the bridge 又换成别的拼写。
约定俗成译名 Tian'anmen Square（注意拼音里的隔音符号），对应 天安门广场。专有地名首字母大写。
音译 + 通名：the Yongding River，对应 永定河。河流名前加定冠词 the，River 首字母大写。
意译 stone lion(s)，对应 石狮。这是全篇高频词，注意它在句中几乎都是复数 stone lions（桥上不止一头），只有 每根柱子上都有一头石狮 这处是单数 a stone lion。

steps.text: 卢沟桥 is 多拱石桥（主语策略：原句主语）中文已有明确主语 卢沟桥。这句中文铺了三个动词性成分（位于、横跨、是），但最核心、定性的是判断句「是…多拱石桥」，所以主干定成 Lugou Bridge is the oldest multi-arch stone bridge，主语 Lugou Bridge、系动词 is、表语 the oldest multi-arch stone bridge。「位于」和「横跨」只是描述位置，降级即可。

位于、横跨降级成分词/独立分句主干之外两块降级安放：位于天安门广场西南15公里处 处理成 located 15 kilometres southwest of Tian'anmen Square（过去分词作状语/可前置）；横跨永定河 处理成 and spans the Yongding River（用 and 接一个并列谓语，或写成 spanning the Yongding River 的现在分词后置定语）。这样三个信息（位置、横跨、定性）就有主有从，而不是三个动词平铺。

时态回指全篇基调用一般现在时：is/spans——这是桥现在仍成立的事实。 最高级冠词最古老的 用最高级 the oldest，最高级前必须加定冠词 the。 方位介词西南15公里处 译 15 kilometres southwest of…，用 southwest of 表「在…西南方」，距离 15 kilometres 置于方位词前。 复合形容词多拱 译 multi-arch（连字符合成的前置定语），arch 用单数作定语；若用 multi-arched 亦可。
Located 15 kilometres southwest of Tian'anmen Square and spanning the Yongding River, Lugou Bridge is the oldest existing multi-arch stone bridge in Beijing.
桥 was built / rebuilt（主语策略：转被动）中文「建成」「重建」「支撑」三个动作的承受者都是桥本身——桥是被建、被重建、被柱子支撑的，没有主动施事者出现，故转被动，把承受者 Lugou Bridge/It 提作主语：It was first built…, rebuilt…, and is supported by 281 pillars。
三动作并列＋柱子作工具最初建成于1192年 与 1698年重建 是两个先后发生的过去动作，用 first built in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698 并列（共享主语）；由281根柱子支撑 是它现在的结构状态，用 is supported by 281 pillars，by 引出施事/支撑物。注意这第三块是「现在仍被支撑」，与前两块的过去动作时态不同，不要一律塞进过去式。

时态建成重建 是过去已完成动作，偏离基调用一般过去时 was built/rebuilt；由281根柱子支撑 是现在仍成立的结构，回到基调用一般现在时被动 is supported。一句之内两种时态，要分清。 语态三处全用被动：was built / was rebuilt / is supported by——桥是被建、被支撑的。 单复数281根柱子 是复数 281 pillars，pillar 加 -s。 时间介词「于1192年/1698年」用 in + 年份：in 1192, in 1698。
It was first built in 1192 and rebuilt in 1698, and is supported by 281 pillars.
There is a stone lion（主语策略：There be）中文 每根柱子上都有一头石狮 表「某处存在某物」，是典型的存在句，用 There be 句型最自然：There is a stone lion on each pillar。主语形式上是 there，真正存在的事物 a stone lion 放在 is 之后。
地点状语后置本句结构简单，主干即全句，只需把 每根柱子上 处理成地点状语 on each pillar 放句末。无多余分句需降级。

时态回指基调用一般现在时 There is——这是桥现在的常态。 主谓一致一头石狮 是单数，There be 的 be 跟其后名词走，故用 is，配单数 a stone lion。 单复数与冠词一头石狮 此处确是单数（每根柱子各一头），用 a stone lion，与下文成群的 stone lions 复数区分开。 分配词每根柱子 用 each pillar（each 后接单数名词），呼应「每根上各有一头」的分配含义。
On each pillar stands a stone lion.

more lions are hidden（主语策略：转被动）中文「藏着更多的狮子」没有明确施事者（不是谁去藏的），重在「更多狮子被藏在某处」这一状态，故转被动，把承受者 more lions 提作主语：More lions are hidden on the head, back, belly or paws…。也可保留 这些石狮 作主语写主动 these stone lions hide more lions，但被动更贴「藏着」的静态含义。
四个部位并列作地点状语头、背、腹部或爪子 是「狮子被藏的位置」，并列成名词串作介词 on 的宾语：on the heads, backs, bellies or paws of these stone lions，用 of 短语把「这些石狮的」处理成后置所属，避免照中文「这些石狮的头背腹爪」语序硬堆在前面。

时态回指基调用一般现在时被动 are hidden——这是石狮现在的样貌常态。 语态用被动 are hidden（更多狮子被藏着）。 单复数这些石狮 复数 these stone lions；部位 heads/backs/bellies/paws 因主体是众多石狮，宜用复数；belly 复数为 bellies（辅音 + y 变 ies）。 并列连词头、背、腹部或爪子 用「或」对应 or 连接最后一项：heads, backs, bellies or paws。
On the heads, backs, bellies or paws of these stone lions are hidden even more lions.
石狮 are 精品（主语策略：原句主语）中文已有明确主语 这些石狮。句中「生动逼真、千姿百态」是描述其状貌的形容性成分，「是…精品」是判断核心，故主干定成判断句 These stone lions are the finest works…，主语 these stone lions、系动词 are、表语 the finest works of stone carving。
形容词组降级成插入语生动逼真、千姿百态 不照中文塞成一串谓语，而降级成插入性的形容词短语：Vivid and lifelike, varying in posture, these stone lions are…（前置形容词状语），或用定语从句 which are vivid and lifelike。这样主干「是精品」清晰，描写作修饰挂在前面。

时态回指基调用一般现在时 are——石狮当下的特征与艺术地位。 主谓一致这些石狮 复数 these stone lions，系动词用 are，表语 the finest works 也用复数呼应。 四字词意译生动逼真 译 vivid and lifelike；千姿百态 不可逐字译，意译为 varying in posture/in a variety of postures，抓「姿态多样」之意。 用词搭配精品 译 the finest works/masterpieces；石刻艺术 译 the stone carving art/the art of stone carving。
Vivid and lifelike, varying in posture, these stone lions are regarded as the finest works of stone carving on Lugou Bridge.

石狮 are countless → 引出谚语（主语策略：原句主语）中文是「原因（石狮不计其数）→ 结果（流传着…说法）」的因果句。前半 桥上的石狮不计其数 以 stone lions 为主语：The stone lions on the bridge are countless/too many to count；后半 北京地区流传着…的说法 表「某说法被流传」，可转被动 a saying… is popular/has spread，或用 there be。两个分句用 so/thus 显因果。

谚语直引＋说法转被动卢沟桥上的石狮子——数不清 是一句民间谚语，作 saying 的内容，用引号直引并意译：the saying "The stone lions on Lugou Bridge are countless"。北京地区流传着…说法 转被动/存在：there is a popular saying in Beijing that…，把「流传着」处理成 popular/widely circulated。

时态回指基调用一般现在时：are countless/there is a saying——这是至今仍成立的事实与仍在流传的说法。 因果连词因而 用 so/thus/therefore 显化因果，不要只用逗号粘连两个独立句（避免 comma splice 病句）。 单复数桥上的石狮 复数 the stone lions；谚语内 lions 亦复数。 用词不计其数 译 countless/too numerous to count/innumerable；数不清 谚语收尾的「数不清」对应 too many to count/impossible to count。
The stone lions on the bridge are too numerous to count, so there is a popular saying in the Beijing area: "The stone lions on Lugou Bridge are simply countless."

卢沟桥 is famous … and is recognized as 丰碑（主语策略：原句主语）中文已有明确主语 卢沟桥。句子是「不仅A，还B」的递进并列：A=以其美学特征闻名于世 → is famous for its aesthetic features；B=被公认为…丰碑 → is recognized as a monument。主干即 Lugou Bridge is not only famous… but also recognized as…，两个表语并列。

两个并列表语共享主语本句无需复杂降级，关键是 not only…but also… 把两个并列谓语/表语挂到同一主语上：is not only famous for its aesthetic features but also recognized as a monument…，避免写成两个独立的 It is famous… It is recognized… 散句。「石桥建筑史上」作 monument 的后置定语 in the history of stone bridge construction。

时态回指基调用一般现在时 is famous/is recognized——其声誉与地位至今成立。 语态被公认为 用被动 is recognized as/is acknowledged as。 介词搭配闻名于世 用 be famous for（因…而闻名）+ its aesthetic features；被公认为 用 be recognized/regarded as + 名词。for 与 as 不可混用。 冠词一座丰碑 是泛指「一座」，用不定冠词 a monument/a landmark。
Lugou Bridge is not only world-famous for its aesthetic features but also widely recognized as a monument in the history of stone bridge construction.
